hypothesis: Lowering the density-weight growth aggressiveness in the overflow-based update (clamping `density_weight_new` to a smaller max and slowing the step-size growth) keeps the analytical placement in a less-congested regime with more whitespace around critical logic, so the single fixed timing-repair pass can insert buffers and shorten detours, reducing TNS across all circuits.
analysis: The hypothesis only partly holds. Two of three cases improved (ariane133-ng45: dTNS +9.5%, dWNS +4.6%; bp-ng45: dTNS +22.2%), consistent with more whitespace easing buffer insertion. But bp_fe-ng45 regressed (dTNS -3.8%, dWNS -1.4%), and the robust mean-std is slightly negative (-0.007), so the gain isn't uniform. Next step: sweep the density-weight cap per circuit family, or make the growth rate adaptive to overflow magnitude, to avoid the bp_fe regression while retaining the ariane/bp gains.
